rationale: Measured structure (current revision de4d95e2, inputs): the step performs exactly 13 fp32 SUM allreduces on process group 0 (12x 28,351,488 B buckets 0-11 for transformer.h.11..h.0 plus one 157,541,376 B bucket 12 for wte/wpe/h.0.ln_1/lm_head; resources.json cross_rank seq 21-33; calls d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1), all RING SIMPLE over SHM/PCIe with 2 channels, peer_access disabled and NVLink not supported (nccl_tuning evidence). collective_calibration measures near-wire per-collective completion at these exact sizes: 1.98 ms per 28 MB bucket and 10.60 ms for the 150 MB bucket, i.e. 12x1.98+10.6 ~= 34.4 ms, while the clean original baseline is rank0 35.70 ms / rank1 45.13 ms (project.json). So on the max rank about 34-36 ms is transport-bound and about 10-11 ms is in-kernel device waiting; the waiting rank flips across captures (rank1 late-early in the clean baseline, rank0 waiting 54.28 ms vs rank1 35.41 ms in the execution_timeline capture), and execution_timeline attributes it to a near-constant ~12.7 ms inter-rank CPU/GPU submission lag on seq 21 plus 0.5-1.9 ms per-bucket readiness jitter on later buckets - not to wire time or algorithm choice. Payload (497,759,232 B/rank), bucket count/cap, DDP wrapper, no_sync schedule and the c10d::allreduce_ sites are frozen in the adapter/invariants, and re-batching buckets would add extra full-payload copies over a ~14.5 GB/s effective transport, so no communication-side edit is a legal or profitable boundary. The only editable cause of the ~10 ms excess is inter-rank readiness skew accumulated over the unsynchronized 3x no_sync microbatches plus the final backward, where host-side Python dispatch is the dominant editable jitter source: python_runtime shows ~608 module _call_impl, 1212 module __getattr__, 536 configuration __getattribute__, 288 eager_router calls per step, with eager GPT2Attention.forward re-doing cache/cross-attention branching, ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS interface lookup and view/split/transpose glue 48x per step, NewGELUActivation.forward at 3.9 ms self time over a pow/mul/tanh op chain, and Conv1D wrapper dispatch 192x. I therefore select the coherent per-layer compute region that schedules gradient readiness for every one of the 13 buckets - GPT2Block (3b09e47895ee88ac921d, 12 instances/48 invocations), all 12 GPT2Attention instance groups, GPT2MLP (ec2154cc4d9de8d016ec), the 4 Conv1D groups (67c824f09e31b34e77c7, 9db63fe3f77e7fb2453e, 2362006c8c4812c12425, 7db6e7ebcaeca9fbb869) and NewGELUActivation (42ca2f3dfd6596c065f5) - as one joint candidate: a lean block-level rewrite needs the attention/MLP/Conv1D/GELU rewrites to be consistent with it (same site set replaced and invoked, per the binding contract's coverage rules), and inlined LayerNorm/Dropout calls keep issuing their unchanged aten kernels. The two allreduce calls are included as affected calls because their durations are the objective this proposal targets; they are not edit sites. Bucket membership links all selected block/Conv1D groups to every bucket 0-11 and the 150 MB bucket (communication-ownership.json), without assigning shared cost.
hypothesis: Replacing the selected per-layer forward path with a host-lean equivalent that issues the identical aten kernel sequence on identical tensors (c_attn/c_proj/c_fc addmm, matmul + mask add, softmax, matmul, layer_norm, tanh-formula NewGELU, p=0 dropout as no-op) removes an estimated 8-14 ms/step of per-rank Python dispatch and its per-op timing variance (python_runtime self-times) while keeping outputs bitwise identical, so gradient values, the exact cross-rank replica check (atol=rtol=0), the serial-reference gradient/parameter checks and the finite-loss/negative controls all pass unchanged. With less host-induced jitter, the two ranks' bucket-readiness times during the final backward align more closely, so the early rank's ncclDevKernel_AllReduce kernels spend less time spinning for the late rank: the max-rank communication_kernel_sum_ms is expected to fall from ~45 ms toward the near-wire level already exhibited by the fast rank (~35-37 ms), a ~15-20% objective reduction, with step_ms not degrading (same GPU kernels, strictly less host work; the 1.05x baseline constraint stays safe). This is a causal hypothesis to be tested, not a prediction of guaranteed benefit: if the ~10 ms skew is driven mainly by non-host factors (OS scheduling, GPU clock variance outside the model), the objective will stay near 45 ms even though step_ms improves; conversely the 3-sample median with max-rank aggregation directly exposes whether the waiting rank's excess tracks the host-path change. Wire-bound floor: the ~34.4 ms calibration sum bounds any achievable objective from below regardless of this edit.
